title: Computational design and functional validation of peptide modulators for AMPAR and NMDAR
content:
Abstract
Ionotropic glutamate receptors AMPAR and NMDAR are central to synaptic transmission and key targets in neurological disease therapy. Here, we developed a de novo design pipeline combining a generative neural network, AlphaFold2 structural predictions, and molecular dynamics to create short, high-affinity, receptor-selective peptide modulators. The algorithm targets receptor hotspots, optimizing for minimal contact distance and high structural confidence, and avoids mode collapse through position-specific scoring matrix integration. In silico evaluation of top candidates exhibited strong binding affinity, low RMSD fluctuations, and stable hydrogen bonding. Selectivity tests confirmed minimal cross-binding between AMPAR- and NMDAR-specific peptides. Top candidates were synthesized and evaluated in in vitro experiments. In rat cortical and hippocampal cultures, peptides induced robust, concentration-dependent intracellular Ca2+ influx, abolished by extracellular calcium removal or selective antagonists (CNQX, MK-801), thus confirming the positive modulatory action of designed peptides. Cross-inhibition assays demonstrated strict receptor specificity. Although calcium responses were lower than those elicited by conventional ligands (α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid and N-methyl-D-aspartate), functional modulation was confirmed. This integrated computational–experimental framework enables efficient development of receptor-specific peptide modulators and offers a promising strategy for therapeutic discovery.
